tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: The account's automations — saved searches that re-run on a schedule and export themselves. Shows each one's niche, cities, cadence, destination, whether it's active, when it next runs, and how the last run went.

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation: re-run a search on a schedule and send the results somewhere automatically. Pass cities as plain strings (e.g. ['Austin, TX', 'Dallas, TX']) — they're resolved for you. tools.name: update_automation
tools.description: Pause an automation (active=false) so it stops running and stops spending leads, or resume it (active=true). Pausing is the safe way to stop an automation you might want back — use delete_automation only when the user wants it gone for good.

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.description: Permanently delete an automation. This cannot be undone — confirm with the user first, and prefer update_automation with active=false if they only want it to stop for now. Leads already collected by past runs are kept; only the schedule is removed.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "export_leads" is 2229 chars, far longer than this server's median (322). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_leads, get_search_results, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Private data: enrich_domains, export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Public sink: search_leads, query_leads, export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation, run_advanced_search · Destructive: search_leads, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_automations, create_automation, delete_automation, find_places, run_advanced_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_leads, get_search_results, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Private data: enrich_domains, export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Public sink: search_leads, query_leads, export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation, run_advanced_search · Destructive: search_leads, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_automations, create_automation, delete_automation, find_places, run_advanced_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
